core_design_principles.rule: Indian wedding invitations establish sacred and familial context before announcing the couple: always place the religious invocation (॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥, ੴ, بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ, or Cross) at the top crown, followed by grandparents'/parents' blessings.
Use a strong architectural silhouette—a Rajputana cusped Jharokha arch, South Indian Gopuram, or Mughal multifoil arch—to frame the couple's names and portrait, creating an immediate sense of place.

Even when all functions occur on the same day (e.g., December 12), assign each ceremony its own visual mood and dress-code swatch: Turmeric/Marigold for Morning Haldi, Pistachio/Leheriya for Noon Mehendi, Crimson/Gold for Sunset Baraat, Indigo/Champagne for Evening Sangeet, and Sindoor Red/Emerald for Night Pheras.

Modern Indian digital invites succeed by combining tactile rituals (tapping a wax seal to open an envelope, showering flower petals, flipping Polaroid story cards, playing gentle Santoor/Shehnai audio) with frictionless utility (one-tap Google Maps links, .ics calendar downloads, and 10-second WhatsApp/web RSVPs).

Maintain a 3.5x to 4x scale ratio between the Couple Names (46-56px display serif/script) and the supporting Date/Venue copy (12-15px), pairing high-contrast serifs (Cinzel, Playfair, Rozha One, Bodoni Moda) with clean geometric sans-serifs (Plus Jakarta Sans, Outfit, Josefin Sans) for addresses and timings.
